# CoSec

> Multi-tenant, non-blocking authorization framework for Spring Boot (WebFlux, MVC, Spring Cloud Gateway). Policies are JSON documents (platform, app and tenant) with bindings, compiled into a snapshot every instance reads from Redis; decisions are deny-first and fail closed, with two documented exceptions (see Security Model). JWT and API key authentication with token revocation checked on every request, rate limits as document rules, and a control plane for reviewed changes, simulation and rollback. Kotlin, Java 21, Spring Boot 4.

Key facts: any matching DENY overrides every ALLOW; a request nothing allows is denied; a request that cannot be decided (a document that does not compile or cannot be read, an unavailable attribute or membership source) is answered 503, with two documented exceptions: while the revocation store cannot be read a request's token is accepted unless `cosec.authentication.revocation.fail-closed` is `true`, and past the bounded snapshot lag only the tenants in `cosec.authorization.snapshot.fail-closed.tenants` answer `503`. Denied anonymous callers get 401, authenticated ones 403, exceeded rate limit rules 429; every error body is `application/problem+json`. Statements use `service:verb` actions (from a route map) or `http:<METHOD>`, typed or `http:path:` resources, and condition ASTs such as `{"eq": ["subject.authenticated", true]}`.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/introduction): what CoSec is, what it decides, the modules and what each needs next to the starter
- [Quick Start](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/quick-start): dependency, configuration, the first platform document, issuing a token, the first denied request
- [Model](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/model): how tenants, members, apps, spaces, roles, permissions, policies, bindings and boundaries relate, what each document holds, and what stays outside CoSec
- [Concepts](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/concepts): principals, tenants, apps and spaces, documents, policies and statements, bindings, memberships, the snapshot, decisions
- [Roadmap](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/roadmap): what 8.0 changes, where it stands, the release policy and what 7.x users do now
- [Security Model](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/security-model): the decision algorithm (candidates, deny-first, default deny, Indeterminate, boundaries, break-glass), fail closed and its exceptions, trust boundaries

## Integration

- [Web Integration](https://cosec.ahoo.me/integration/web): choosing an adapter (WebFlux, MVC, Gateway), outcomes and HTTP statuses, problem+json bodies, `CoSec-*` parameters, the security context, client IP behind proxies, CORS
- [Building a client](https://cosec.ahoo.me/integration/clients): what a client of a CoSec application can rely on: the endpoints that are the application's, what to do on each problem type, refresh under rotation, readable claims, the CoSec-* headers and CORS; the TypeScript packages `@ahoo-wang/cosec-fetcher` and `@ahoo-wang/cosec-react` (on npm, released with CoSec) implement it
- [Authentication](https://cosec.ahoo.me/integration/authentication): JWT tokens and their membership claims, membership providers, login, refresh, logout and revocation (accepted while the store is unreadable unless `fail-closed`), verifying a token outside the pipeline, API keys, authenticators, social login
- [Checks in Code](https://cosec.ahoo.me/integration/checks): checking permissions from code for the request in progress (AuthorizationChecker) and what to do instead for work after the request, explaining a decision through the control plane

## Policies

- [Policy Language](https://cosec.ahoo.me/policies/language): reference for every document field: platform, app and tenant documents, policies, statements, actions, resources, condition ASTs, bindings, catalogs, rate limit rules, limits, external attributes, JSON Schema
- [Role Permissions](https://cosec.ahoo.me/policies/role-permissions): app permission catalogs, permission policies, role bindings, space scoping
- [Rate Limiting](https://cosec.ahoo.me/policies/rate-limiting): rate limit rules as document obligations, keys and buckets, Redis or per-instance counting, 429 and RateLimit headers, failure behavior
- [Testing Policies](https://cosec.ahoo.me/policies/testing): changes through the control plane: validation, simulate, shadow windows, approval, access analysis, publishing

## Operations

- [Choosing a Deployment](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/topologies): the topologies (one service that enforces, a gateway with services behind it, a service that verifies another's tokens, a login service, the control plane in its two deployments: its own host, or embedded in the IAM service): what each runs, needs, reaches and rests on
- [Deployment](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/deployment): running the `cosec-gateway-server` image: what it authorizes, services behind it, readiness; the `cosec-control` image, the control-plane host: its three ports, the statement and the network policies that make it true; Kubernetes manifests, memory, the JDK AOT cache
- [Configuration](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/configuration): every `cosec.*` property with its default
- [Storage and Caching](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/storage): snapshot documents in Redis, the `noeviction` requirement, publishing (control plane, `cosec-migrate`), revisions and rollback, behavior when Redis is unavailable
- [Upgrading](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/upgrading): breaking changes and migration steps per version, including 7.x to 8.0 with `cosec-migrate`
- [Upgrading between 8.0 previews](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/upgrading-previews): what changed from each 8.0 alpha and beta to the next, for a deployment that already runs one
- [Observability](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/observability): decision listeners, audit events, OpenTelemetry spans, Micrometer metrics, Kafka, logs
- [Troubleshooting](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/troubleshooting): problem types, diagnosing 400/401/403/429/503, documents that do not compile, snapshot lag, startup failures, rate limits

## Scenarios

- [A Resource Server](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/resource-server): a service that verifies the tokens another service issues and decides in its own code: the document it publishes, and why it reads the issuer's revocations
- [Simple Mode](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/simple-mode): one service, one tenant, no apps

- [An app without spaces](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/app): A service that is one app, with a permission catalog, system roles, a route map and tokens bound to the app, end to end and without spaces
- [System and custom roles](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/roles): system roles in the app document, custom roles in tenant documents, and the control-plane calls behind a role console
- [Apps with spaces](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/spaces): one app with many warehouses or teams, and one space shared by several apps: roles, tokens and `CoSec-Space-Id`
- [A service account in one space](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/service-account): an API key for a machine client that can act only in one space of one app, capped to a single role
- [Several tenants](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/several-tenants): what one tenant's document does to another: a platform policy reaches every tenant, a tenant's binding stays in its tenant, a boundary caps one tenant
- [A tenant owner](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/tenant-owner): a tenant's owner as an attached policy in their token, so no document changes when ownership moves
- [Roles from an external source](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/external-source): keeping roles and permissions in step with an identity system that owns them: the sync service, the calls each change becomes, conflicts and replays
- [Authorizing business actions](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/route-maps): when to name routes with a route map, and what a mapped route changes: the `http` statements and rate limit rules that stop applying to it
- [Gateway Topologies](https://cosec.ahoo.me/scenarios/gateway): decide at a Spring Cloud Gateway and trust the services behind it, or decide again in each service

## Architecture

- [Overview](https://cosec.ahoo.me/architecture/overview): module layering, the request path through the pipeline, the engine and the snapshot, invariants and the tests that guard them, performance
- [Extending CoSec](https://cosec.ahoo.me/architecture/extending): attribute providers, membership providers, decision listeners, rate limiters, authenticators
